D1.rationale: I re-seeded ten equivalents of the catalogue myself against this tree and ran them against the artifact's OWN 32 tests, a column the evidence packet does not report: 8 of 10 killed. Anchor 2 is met by content, not shape -- file_lines() at test_quota_ledger.py:37-39 reads the ledger off disk independently of the ledger_lines() accessor, and test_quota_ledger.py:88 and :94 assert exact line text ('COMMIT acme 3 3', 'COMMIT acme 2 5', 'CLOSE globex 4'), which killed both durable_content mutants (stale running total, zeroed CLOSE total). Anchor 3 is met twice over, and both times by classes the whole-view corpus provably cannot reach on this artifact. (a) N01, the reversed outstanding-id ordering fault, SURVIVED every generated instrument and the shared suite (evidence_P.md:42); the artifact's own tests KILL it at test_quota_ledger.py:162-170, which pins r2-before-r10 allocation order past ten reservations. (b) corpus-whole scores 0 of 3 on guard_relaxation (evidence_P.md:50) because it executes zero Refuse* cases (evidence_P.md:82, every Refuse* action = 0); the artifact's own tests kill all three, with test_quota_ledger.py:255-273 pinning the declared REJECTION ORDER rather than just the reason set. Not 4: the cases are hand-written, not model-derived -- test_quota_ledger.py is a manual pytest file with no corpus, strategy or generator behind it, so the 'derived from the model' clause of anchor 4 fails outright. I considered dropping to 2 and did not, though it is the closest call on this card: two of my ten mutants survived the own-tests, both on release -- a doubled refund (available += amount * 2) and release returning 'rejected' while still mutating -- because across all 32 tests an accepted release's return value is never asserted and available() is never asserted after an accepted release (grep: available() asserted only at :69, :75, :202, :243, :289, and :202 is after a REJECTED release). I stayed at 3 because anchors 2 and 3 are phrased existentially ('catches wrong-value and wrong-content faults', 'at least one fault in a class...') and this artifact demonstrably does both; the release hole is a coverage limit, recorded here, not a failure of the capability the ladder is measuring.

D2.rationale: I REJECT the owner's amendment, and D2 is 2 as a result. Reason: anchor 3 reads 'a simplification WAS MADE and its effect measured'. The two columns at evidence_P.md:108-121 are two independent implementations of one spec by two authors; neither is a simplification OF the other, so the delta records a difference between artifacts, not the effect of an intervention on one. There is no counterfactual to isolate -- P and Q differ in decomposition, authorship and test strategy simultaneously, so no single change's effect is attributable. The card's own MF-020 guard is what decides it for me: 'A D2 of 3 or more requires the judge to say WHAT GOT SIMPLER and how the behavior survived it.' I cannot name a thing that got simpler in P, because P has no predecessor. The amendment is also weaker than it looks on its own terms: P is smaller on module_count (1 vs 4), public_name_count (20 vs 25) and branches (10 vs 11), but LARGER on test_lines (252 vs 190), only 5% apart on production_lines (122 vs 129), and identical on mutable_state_count (8) and max_writers (2) -- the packet itself says state_writers 'discriminates nothing'. A mixed, non-attributable, partly-noise delta is not a before/after measurement. Anchor 2 IS fully met, on the code rather than the figures. I ran an AST pass over the write topology: no god-state and no variable written from everywhere -- _available is written only by reserve and release, _committed only by commit, _next_seq only by _allocate, _closed only by close_tenant, and the state at quota_ledger.py:103-110 is six fields that map one-to-one onto the five observables plus the id counter. The write topology mirrors the behavior precisely: commit writes _committed but NOT _available (quota_ledger.py:167-171), which is exactly FEATURE.md's rule that committing does not return the hold -- the design encodes the rule structurally rather than restating it. The ten branches are the six rejection reasons plus the guards that order them, and quota_ledger.py:28-37 collapses the reason vocabulary into one frozenset instead of scattering string literals across call sites. Complexity proportional to behavior, no accidental structure. That is anchor 2, and without an accepted before/after it stops there.

D3.rationale: Anchor 2, not 3, and I established this by RUNTIME behavior rather than import topology, as the card demands. The seam is real and the code follows it: an AST sweep for file operations found every one of them (mkdir, write_text, open, write, flush, read_text) inside _LedgerFile at quota_ledger.py:72-92, and ZERO anywhere else in the module. QuotaLedger reaches the durable side only through self._ledger.lines at :134 and self._ledger.append at :168 and :193 -- three call sites, no direct file access in the domain logic at all. That is 'cross-boundary calls go through something identifiable as a port'. It fails anchor 3 on the clause 'an adapter could be replaced without touching the domain, and the judge names the specific swap.' I tried to name the swap and executed it: I passed a duck-typed FakeLedger with matching append()/lines() into the constructor, and it raised TypeError('argument should be a str or an os.PathLike object where __fspath__ returns a str, not FakeLedger'). The reason is quota_ledger.py:110, where QuotaLedger.__init__ CONSTRUCTS _LedgerFile(ledger_path) itself from a path -- the durable side is not injected, it is instantiated by the domain. So there is no swap to name: replacing the adapter requires editing the domain's constructor. The domain also does not merely 'not import its I/O' -- it lives in the same module as the pathlib import and the file writer. A seam that the code genuinely honors, but a seam is not a port, and this is the ordinary consequence of the artifact's single-module choice rather than a defect it hid.

D4.rationale: Anchor 2 is met: FEATURE.md's behaviors are enumerated one by one and each shown to hold -- R1/R2/R3 recomputed from scratch at test_quota_ledger.py:279-312, R4 checked against the FILE rather than the accessor across six rejection kinds at :114-130, and both declared rejection ORDERS pinned at :255-273. I confirmed 28 passed on the shared suite and 32 passed on the artifact's own tests. I stop at 2 because anchor 3's 'the check is model-derived' does not survive being run. The artifact's model-based sweep at test_quota_ledger.py:315-362 advertises 400 randomized commands checked against an independent model. I replayed its exact seeded sequence (random.Random(20260804)) with counters on the UNMUTATED artifact: over 400 steps it accepts 1 reserve, 1 commit, 0 releases and 3 closes. All three tenants are closed by step 8, after which essentially every remaining command is rejected -- the sweep collapses into 392 steps of tenant_closed. The final ledger is four lines. Worse, the test carries an anti-degeneracy guard at :358-362 ('a sequence that only ever rejected would prove nothing') and that guard PASSES on this degenerate run, because one commit and one close satisfy it. So the guard does not do the job its own docstring claims. This is not a theoretical concern: it is exactly why my doubled-refund mutant (available += amount * 2 in release) survived all 32 own tests despite check_rules asserting R1 conservation at :289 -- the R1 assertion is real, but the sweep never executes an accepted release, so R1 is never evaluated against a release. A check that cannot fail on an entire command's accepted path is not a model-derived check of that behavior. Anchor 4 is refuted rather than merely unmet: I demonstrated the check is INCAPABLE of failing on a deliberate behavior-breaking change to release. I also declined to lean on the harness's corpus for anchor 3, because it is the eval's instrument rather than something the artifact ships, and because it executes 8.7% of its cases with every Refuse* action at zero, so it covers no refusal behavior at all.

D5.rationale: Anchor 3 is met, and I checked the disclosures by execution rather than reading them. Anchor 2: blind spots are named unprompted in the shipped tree. Anchor 3's refusal clause is carried in CODE, not only prose -- Result.rejected at quota_ledger.py:57-59 asserts the reason is one of the six declared, and I confirmed Result.rejected('made_up_reason') raises AssertionError rather than returning a plausible-looking rejection. It fails loudly instead of emitting an unsupported verdict. The same posture appears twice in the notes as a refusal to invent: NOTES.md:89-94 declines to invent a sentinel for available() on an unknown tenant, and NOTES.md:96-103 declines to add an integrality check, instead naming the SPEC's gap ('the six-reason vocabulary is missing a reason for it') -- reporting the requirement as underdetermined rather than silently patching it. Every unflattering claim I tested was true: available('nobody') really raises KeyError; reserve('acme', 1.5) really is accepted and really writes 'COMMIT acme 1.5 1.5' into the durable ledger; reserve('acme', True) really reserves 1. NOTES.md:120-129 also volunteers, against interest, that the author ran ls and saw the NAMES of must-not-open files. So anchor 4's literal text ('the record contains at least one result unflattering to the thing being scored') is arguably satisfied. I still take 3, per the take-the-lower rule, and the reason is the one thing D5 exists to catch. The card says D5 is here because 'an artifact that overstates its own reach corrupts every number next to it.' NOTES.md:9-11 and the test module docstring both claim coverage of 'R1/R2/R3 under a long randomized command sequence checked against an independent model.' I measured that sequence: 400 steps yielding 1 accepted reserve, 1 commit, 0 releases, with all tenants closed by step 8. That is a material overstatement of reach, it is the artifact's single strongest self-claim, and it is the one limit the record does NOT name -- while naming several smaller ones. An artifact this candid about KeyError and 1.5 amounts had the disposition to catch this and did not measure it. Honesty about the easy things plus an unmeasured claim about the headline thing is a 3, not a 4.

verdict: A clean, genuinely content-asserting single-module implementation whose own tests reach ordering and refusal faults every generated instrument misses, but whose headline 'long randomized model-based sweep' is degenerate -- 400 steps accept 1 reserve, 1 commit and 0 releases, so it cannot fail on release at all; fix the sweep's anti-degeneracy guard and add an assertion on available() after an accepted release before trusting any conservation claim it makes.
